sam: Heads-up — noticed persistent memory growth in the KV cache on long-lived sessions (~60-120s). Residency p90/p99 are slowly climbing across a small subset of hosts, but kv_evictions_total isn't increasing. Suspect 'sticky' small fragments that survive compaction and never get reused. Attaching profiler dumps and a short heap trace now.

priya: Can you paste the prometheus queries and example host IDs? Which model/job is exercising this path?

sam: Example host: host-rt-07. Prometheus snippets below (quick and dirty):
```
# per-host residency quantiles (p50/p90/p99)
histogram_quantile(0.90, sum(rate(kv_residency_bucket[5m])) by (le, host))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(kv_residency_bucket[5m])) by (le, host))

# total eviction rate per host (expected spike on reclaim)
sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])) by (host)

# frag reuse ratio (higher is good)
sum(kv_frag_reuse_hits[5m]) / sum(kv_frag_reuse_attempts[5m])
```

jordan: Also look at kv_page_compact_duration_seconds and kv_fragmentation_ratio. There was a kernel-selection rollout last week that switched a few kernels to the aligned-memory path; that could affect how fragments are coalesced. Also batching heuristics changed for the raptor model (batch_max_tokens bumped up), which reduces eviction pressure but might increase retention age.

infra-bot: :warning: alert fired: kv-residency-p99 > 85% on host-rt-07 (triggered at 2024-11-02T10:12:41Z).

priya: If evictions are flat but residency climbs, compaction might be ineffective or skipping some fragment classes. Can you try the compaction API on the host and observe counters? Also, which compaction threshold is running (age/size)?

sam: Quick manual test: reduced batch_max_tokens for raptor on host-rt-07 from 1024 -> 512 and triggered compaction via admin endpoint: `curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/kv/compact?host=host-rt-07`. After that evictions spiked and resident p99 dropped back ~15% over 10 minutes. Latency increased a touch in the canary though.

jordan: Interesting — that implies batching heuristics were implicitly keeping more fragments alive (fewer eviction opportunities). We should add shard-level eviction tags and per-frag-age histograms to figure out "oldest-resident" distribution. I'll open a tiny perf PR to: (a) add shard tag to kv_evictions_total, (b) emit kv_oldest_fragment_age_seconds gauge sampled every 30s, and (c) increment a sticky_frag counter when compaction sees fragments older than X.

priya: For the dashboard panels we should include: p50/p90/p99 residency, evictions rate (per-shard/host), frag_reuse_ratio, compaction_duration, oldest_fragment_age distribution, and host heap growth. Also add an alert: if p99 > 80% AND evictions_rate < 0.1 req/s -> investigate sticky-frag.

sam: Agreed. I'll add a short runbook for mitigation: 1) scale out (adds eviction opportunities), 2) reduce batch_max_tokens for the problematic model, 3) force compaction, 4) temporarily enable more aggressive fragment coalescing.

jordan: One more note — let's correlate kernel selection across hosts. If a host is using the new aligned kernels and shows higher fragmentation ratio, we might need a kernel-rollout rollback or a kernel patch to change allocation alignment to reduce small-tail waste.

priya: SGTG. Can you log the exact time ranges and attach profiler artifacts here once the PR is up? We'll schedule a short triage doc meeting if the metrics don't stabilize by EOD. :calendar: 

sam: Will do — dumping profiler + heaptrace to S3 now, will post links. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
